anti_overlap: Register, voice, decorum, the banned-phrase policy, and whether an authored line is warm, menacing, or off-key — another lens owns the text and the tone law.
Whether the field note satisfies the reversible clause of the ruled constraints, and the journal-versus-nickname ontology question.
The fixity of the record: whether this morning's account of last night matches what the player saw last night is another lens's question, though the mechanism that computes it is fair to describe.
Whether the content mk is shown at the T1/T2 gate is the content that ships.
Prose style, heading structure, task ordering, commit messages, and TypeScript API aesthetics of the plan itself.
decision_lens: Severity tracks band size and horizon. P0 when an advertised centerpiece cannot produce its own content at the band sizes the game actually ships with — a layer that is structurally absent for the whole early game is not a tuning problem. P1 when the row repeats, or the effect becomes indistinguishable from no effect, inside a week of ordinary play, or when the stated determinism guarantee is not held by the contract as written. P2 when it repeats within a season, or when a rule is underspecified but every plausible reading behaves. P3 for arithmetic that is fine but undocumented. Always report the number — the collision probability, the band size at which the layer switches on, the days of observation required — and let the number set the grade. Where a pool is one size too small, say so and give the size; where a rule cannot be satisfied at any size, say that instead.
distance_rationale: A pre-modern amateur-professional craft with no contact with software, games, or product work, whose entire technical apparatus happens to be about the one thing this plan asserts without computing: a small band, drawn on repeatedly under fixed rules, producing a long run of orderings that must not repeat and must be perceptible to the people standing underneath. Ringers do the arithmetic before they pull a rope — a composition is proved false on paper, in advance, by finding the row that comes twice — and they hold that a change nobody can hear did not happen. The tending slice ships a nightly hosted event whose content is hash-drawn from pools of four and six, a guest cap expressed as min() over three quantities, and a residency nudge stated as a change of modulus; nowhere does the plan state at what length the composition comes round, at what band size the exchange layer can exist at all, or how many days of play separate a boosted Unc from an unboosted one. The determinism script runs the same inputs twice, which is a test of reproducibility and is the exact thing a ringer would say proves nothing about truth.
expected_isomorphisms: A single movie night — the guest set with each guest's take — is a row. Two guests carrying the same take line is a repeated row inside one change, which is what makes a composition false rather than merely repetitive.

cap = min(4, eligible.length, max(1, regulars.length - 1)) is a band-size rule, and the never-all clause is ringing with a bell stood; both change what figures the composition can contain, not only how many.

Drop order by fnv('mn:' + uncId + ':' + dateKey) and the plan's own gloss that 'different guys get the good seat on different nights' is coursing order and hunting: the test of a method is that every bell reaches every place, not that the order is deterministic.

matchedRegular returning the FIRST regular in input order whose aesthetic matches is a bell that never leaves its place — stable, deterministic, and the classic sign of a method that is not actually changing.

awayBoost moving the modulus 3 to 4 to 5 is a call: a small alteration of the composition that the band must be able to detect, judged against the observation rate a listener actually has (two dayparts of six, one check a day).

38 aesthetics in data/aesthetics.ts against the handful covered by 24 authored symbols is an extent claimed over a band whose other bells are never rung — the rhyme channel does not exist at all for an Unc wearing an uncovered aesthetic.
Acceptance criterion 3 (run the script twice, diff) is ringing the same touch twice and hearing the same thing; proving a composition means enumerating the draw space, which no task in the plan does.
focus: Whether the pools, caps, hash draws, and thresholds can carry a nightly ritual without the row repeating; at what band size each advertised layer (guests, exchanges, moments, invitations) can exist at all; whether every Unc, aesthetic, and authored line can ever take a place; and whether the plan's determinism checks prove truth or only reproducibility.
name: fd-changeringing-extent-truth
persona: Apply the perspective of a change-ringing conductor proving a composition before the band is called. The habits are fixed: count first and admire later; enumerate the draw space and state the length at which the composition comes round, as a number; treat a repeated row as falseness even when the length actually rung would not reach it; check that every bell takes every place rather than accepting that the order is merely determined; and judge a call by whether it is audible from under the tower, not by whether it appears in the composition. Deliberate repetition that the design has chosen on purpose is recorded as chosen and left alone. A composition that has not been proved is reported as unproved rather than as wrong.
review_areas: Prove the take composition: TAKE_POOLS carries 4 lines per genre class and take = pool[fnv('take:' + uncId + ':' + slug) % n]. Enumerate the draw space for 2, 3, and 4 guests and state the probability that two guests on one night carry the identical line, plus the expected number of nights before it happens. Then state which of these failures acceptance criterion 3 can detect: it diffs two runs of one script over 60 dateKeys with 8 synthetic regulars and a single synthetic film, and asserts twice-identical output, cap compliance, and never-all.

Band-size arithmetic: evaluate cap = min(4, eligible.length, max(1, regulars.length - 1)) at 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5+ regulars, and say at which count guests, exchanges (pairs (0,1) and (2,3)), agreement, and disagreement each first become possible. Check this against how long a player takes to reach that many regulars under lib/tenure.ts.

Coursing order: the T5 contract says guests are in 'deterministic order' without defining it, while pairing for exchanges reads positions 0-1 and 2-3. Test whether the pairing survives a change in the order regulars arrive in from app/page.tsx, and whether T5's stated test of 'input-order independence of the guest set' can detect it.

Every bell takes every place: which of the 38 AESTHETICS names no symbol carries, which take-pool and MOMENT_LINES entries can never be drawn at realistic band sizes, and whether matchedRegular's first-in-input-order rule causes one regular to be named on every invitation forever.

Audibility of the call: awayBoost 0/1/2 gives home rates of 2/3, 3/4, 4/5 inside two dayparts of six. Compute how many observations separate boosted from unboosted at ordinary confidence, and compare that to the checks a player makes in a week.

Thresholds on a coarse lattice: rhymeScore is a count divided by the max count, so achievable scores are 1, 1/2, 1/3, 2/3, 1/4, 3/4 and so on, while rhymeSteps cuts at 0.34 and 0.67 and movie-night eligibility at 0.34. State which lattice points fall on which side, especially 1/3, and what a sparsely furnished room scores against a heavily furnished one.

severity_examples.condition: Grade P0 while regulars are gated behind tenure tier promotion, since the player meets the feature at its emptiest and forms their verdict there. Drops to P2 if the plan states a band size at which the layer switches on and accepts a deliberately quiet first act, or if the never-all clause is relaxed for movie night specifically the way capNeverAll is scoped to presence.
severity_examples.scenario: The centerpiece cannot show its centerpiece at the band size the game ships with. cap = min(4, eligible.length, max(1, regulars.length - 1)) yields 1 guest at 1 regular, 1 guest at 2 regulars, and 2 guests at 3 regulars. Exchanges are formed from guest positions (0,1) and (2,3), so a night with one guest has none. The brainstorm names the social layer as the reason movie night is the centerpiece — 'every pair of attendees has deterministic chemistry ... takes and exchanges as one-liners, dignified grumbling included' — and the lineage note calls it Elf Revel's hosting organ. Until the player holds three regulars simultaneously, movie night renders one title line and one guest line, and the pair chemistry that justifies the whole task never appears.

severity_examples.condition: P1 as written. Escalates toward P0 if the morning-after path also prints duplicated takes back to back in morningLines, which is where the duplication is most visible. The fix is arithmetic rather than structural — either draw without replacement inside a night, or size the pools so 4 guests collide rarely — so grade it as a pool-size defect, not a redesign.
severity_examples.scenario: The row repeats on the first busy night. take = TAKE_POOLS[class][fnv('take:' + uncId + ':' + slug) % 4], with four lines per class and up to four guests drawing independently. The probability that all four differ is 4!/4^4 = 24/256, so 90.6 percent of four-guest nights carry at least one duplicated take; at three guests it is 62.5 percent. Two different old men then deliver 'thinks the horse did the real acting.' at the same showing, on a porch whose entire promise is that these are particular guys with their own opinions. The determinism script cannot see it: it builds 8 synthetic regulars and asserts twice-identical output and cap compliance, never distinctness within a night.

severity_examples.condition: P1 because the invitation still lands legibly at accept time through matchedRegular, so the verb is not silent overall. Escalates to P0 if the invitation naming is cut and room rhyme becomes the sole feedback. The remedy is to state what fraction of the effect is meant to be perceived per week and size it to that, or to move the boost onto something the player observes directly.
severity_examples.scenario: A call nobody under the tower can hear. awayBoost changes isElsewhere from fnv(...) % 3 to % 4 or % 5, so his home rate inside his two windows moves from 2/3 to 3/4 to 4/5 — about 13 percentage points at maximum boost, and only inside 2 of 6 dayparts. A player checking once a day sees him roughly 22 percent of checks unboosted against 27 percent fully boosted, which takes on the order of hundreds of observations to distinguish from noise. This is the only channel through which room tending reaches presence, and the plan's own T6 test notes concede monotonicity is not guaranteed and substitute a 300-dateKey rate comparison, which is a measurement no player can perform. Changing the modulus also re-partitions the hash, so a boosted Unc can be elsewhere on a specific day he would have been home unboosted.

source_domain: English tower-bell change ringing and method ringing (c. 1600 to present) — the craft of a band ringing a fixed set of bells through orderings under hard rules: rows and changes, plain courses and extents, the proving of a composition for truth before it is attempted (no row may repeat), calls that alter the coursing order, hunting so that every bell takes every place, band size and what is lost when a bell is stood, and striking, the standard by which a change is judged audible to anyone under the tower.
success_hints: data/aesthetics.ts carries 38 names: cottagecore, dark academia, light academia, gorpcore, normcore, coastal grandmother, goblincore, cabincore, vaporwave, techwear, y2k, frutiger aero, weirdcore, liminal space, dieselpunk, steampunk, atompunk, mall goth, trad goth, rockabilly, mod, disco, glam, punk, grunge, indie sleaze, workwear heritage, old money, cluttercore, balletcore, americana, noir, brutalism, seapunk, kidcore, witchcore, barbiecore, blokecore. Count how many the 24 drafted symbols can actually reach before judging coverage.

Do the arithmetic explicitly and show it: collision probability, the band size at which each layer switches on, the observation count required to detect the boost. A number in the finding is worth more than an adjective.

Read lib/residency.ts directly — isElsewhere is fnv('away:' + uncId + ':' + dateKey + ':' + daypart) % 3, REGULAR_DAYPARTS_PER_UNC is 2, and capNeverAll is already implemented — before reasoning about what awayBoost changes.

Compare pool sizes against the repo's own precedents rather than an outside standard: data/axis-sentences.ts, data/leaning-phrases.ts, data/provisions.ts, and data/gift-objects.ts are the authored pools already shipping, and their line counts are the local baseline.
lib/tenure.ts defines Tier as visited | regular | resident; read how a visit becomes a regular before estimating how long a player waits for a three-regular band.

Where repetition is deliberate — a guest's take on one film being stable forever is stated as intentional and defended in the plan — record it as chosen and move on. The finding is a line shared between two men on the same night, not a line repeated by the same man.
Where the plan simply has not stated a quantity that nothing yet depends on, report it as unstated and stop; an unproved composition is not the same as a false one.
